name: Real-Time Widget for Matomo
author: JRMora

sections.description:
This plugin adds a native widget to the WordPress dashboard that connects to your Matomo On-Premise installation to display vital metrics in real-time.

Unlike other plugins that use iframes (often blocked for security) or synchronous PHP requests (which slow down the admin area), this widget uses a 100% JavaScript (Client-Side) architecture.

Your WordPress server performs no requests; the browser queries your Matomo API directly.

Key Features:

  • Zero Server Impact: All processing is done in the client’s browser.
  • Pure Real-Time: Visitor counters and logs update automatically every 10 seconds.
  • Smart Hybrid Chart: Combines historical data (cached) with real-time data from the current day for total accuracy.
  • Performance Monitor: Detailed chart of load times (Network, Server, DOM…) and visit duration metrics.
  • “Black Box” Tooltips: Detailed, accessible information on hover, with visual differentiation for Searches, Downloads, Outlinks, and Events.
  • Deep Links: Direct access to the visitor profile and actions in your Matomo dashboard.
  • Desktop Alerts: Native browser notifications with sound when traffic exceeds your configured threshold.

Note: This plugin requires a self-hosted Matomo installation (On-Premise) and a read-only Auth Token.

sections.installation:
1. Upload the real-time-widget-for-matomo folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to Settings > Matomo Widget.
  4. Enter your Matomo URL (e.g., https://yourserver.com/stats/), your Site ID (usually 1), and your Auth Token.
  5. Go to the Dashboard and enjoy your stats.
sections.faq:
Does it work with Matomo Cloud?

This plugin is designed and tested for On-Premise installations (hosted on your own server).
While it might technically work with the cloud version if CORS headers are correctly configured on the target server, we do not offer official support for that configuration.

Does the widget slow down my WordPress admin?

No. Unlike other plugins, this widget does not make requests from your server (PHP).
All data loading is done asynchronously from your browser (JavaScript) once the page has loaded, so your server performance remains intact.

Why do I need to create an Auth Token?

To allow the widget to securely read your Matomo data without exposing your administrator password.
We recommend creating a specific token just for this widget with read-only permissions.

Why don’t alerts sound (or appear) on my mobile?

Mobile browsers freeze background tabs or when the screen is off to save battery. Additionally, they require constant interaction to allow sound playback. This widget is designed as a desktop tool to keep on a second screen or pinned tab while you work.

Can I use my own alert sound?

Yes. You can replace the alerta.mp3 file found in the plugin folder (/wp-content/plugins/real-time-widget-for-matomo/) with your own MP3 file, provided you keep the exact same filename.
Important: Browsers aggressively cache audio files. If you replace the file but still hear the old sound, you must clear your browser cache (or test in incognito mode) to load the new sound.
sections.changelog:
1.4.0

  • Fix: Renamed all functions, classes, and database options to use a unique 5-letter prefix (rtwfm_) to comply with WordPress.org guidelines and prevent conflicts.
  • Update: Refactored global JavaScript variables to use the new prefix.
  • Improvement: Made the plugin fully translation-ready by localizing all remaining hardcoded strings in JavaScript (Tooltips, Chart labels, etc).

1.3.0

  • Security: Refactored plugin structure to separate JS/CSS assets from the main PHP file.
  • Security: Implemented wp_enqueue_script and wp_localize_script for secure data handling.
  • Update: Updated Chart.js library to version 4.5.1 (latest stable).

1.2.1

  • Fix: Corrected Referrer Type detection logic to handle string values (e.g., ‘search’, ‘website’) returned by Matomo API, fixing the issue where all traffic appeared as ‘Direct Entry’.

1.2.0

  • New: Local sound (mp3) implementation to avoid external resource blocking (CORS/403).
  • Improvement: Native integration with get_site_icon_url() to use the Site Icon (Favicon) in desktop alerts instead of the generic WP logo.
  • Improvement: Smart logic to handle modern browser ‘Autoplay’ policies (audio unlock via interaction).
  • Improvement: Updated test script in settings to reflect the real environment.
  • Fix: Added error handling (try/catch) in notifications to prevent the widget from crashing on mobile browsers (Illegal constructor error).

1.1.0

  • New: “Clean Uninstall” option in settings to remove the token and database configuration upon plugin deletion.
  • New: uninstall.php file to handle data cleanup.
  • Updated: Compatibility tested up to WordPress 6.9.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Support for Hybrid Charts (Chart.js).
  • Performance Monitor.
  • Visitor Log with semantic icons (Pageview, Download, Outlink, Search, Event).
